verses.zh: 亚哈有七十个儿子在撒马利亚。耶户写信送到撒马利亚，通知耶斯列的首领，就是长老和教养亚哈众子的人，说：
verses.en: Ahab had 70 sons living in Samaria.[NOTE:1] So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria to the leading officials of Jezreel and to the guardians of Ahab’s dynasty. This is what the letters said,[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

Heb “to the officers of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying.” It is not certain why the officials of Jezreel would be in Samaria. They may have fled there after they heard what happened to Joram and before Jehu entered the city. They would have had time to flee while Jehu was pursuing Ahaziah.
verses.commentary:
10:1 "Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria" This was a round number which would include all male
descendants and relatives (i.e., Jdgs. 9:5; 12:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

▣ "Jehu" This is a form of the sacred name YHWH (cf. Exod. 3:14). This particular form seems to mean
"He is."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "wrote letters and sent them to. . ." Notice the different groups.

- the rulers (BDB 978)

- chieftain

- ruler

- official

- captain

- prince

- the elders (BDB 278, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS)

- the guardians (BDB 52, KB 63, Qal PARTICIPLEe, "those who nourish")

- this group of leaders is labeled in a different way in v. 5

▣ "to the rulers of Jezreel" The Septuagint has "the rulers of Samaria." There is a problem in the
Hebrew text because it is incongruent that Jehu, who was in Jezreel, would write to Jezreel.

The JPSOA footnote suggests an emendation from "of Jezreel" to "of the city" (Vulgate). Another
possibility is that the leaders of Jezreel fled to Samaria with the relatives of Ahab and Jezebel.

verses.zh: 「你们那里既有你们主人的众子和车马、器械、坚固城，
verses.en: “You have with you the sons of your master, chariots and horses, a fortified city, and weapons. So when this letter arrives,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And now when this letter comes to you—with you are the sons of your master and with you are chariots and horses and a fortified city and weapons.”
verses.commentary:
10:2 Jehu is attempting to have the male descendants of Ahab killed, but to do it in such a way as not to
draw the displeasure of the populace to himself.

verses.zh: 接了这信，就可以在你们主人的众子中选择一个贤能合宜的，使他坐他父亲的位，你们也可以为你们主人的家争战。」
verses.en: pick the best and most capable[NOTE:1] of your master’s sons, place him on his father’s throne, and defend[NOTE:2] your master’s dynasty.”
notes: Hebrew יָשָׁר (yashar) does not have its normal moral/ethical nuance here (“upright”), but a more neutral sense of “proper, right, suitable.” For the gloss “capable,” see HALOT 450 s.v. יָשָׁר.
Or “fight for.”

verses.zh: 他们却甚惧怕，彼此说：「二王在他面前尚且站立不住，我们怎能站得住呢？」
verses.en: They were absolutely terrified[NOTE:1] and said, “Look, two kings could not stop him![NOTE:2] How can we?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “they were very, very afraid.” The term מְאֹד (meʾod) “very,” is repeated for emphasis.
Heb “did not stand before him.”
Heb “How can we stand?”
verses.commentary:
10:4 "the two kings did not stand before him" This is the rationalization of the leaders of Samaria in
surrendering to Jehu. The two rulers referred to are Joram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah (cf. chapter 9).

verses.zh: 家宰、邑宰，和长老，并教养众子的人，打发人去见耶户，说：「我们是你的仆人，凡你所吩咐我们的都必遵行，我们不立谁作王，你看怎样好就怎样行。」
verses.en: So the palace supervisor,[NOTE:1] the city commissioner,[NOTE:2] the leaders,[NOTE:3] and the guardians sent this message to Jehu, “We are your subjects![NOTE:4] Whatever you say, we will do. We will not make anyone king. Do what you consider proper.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the one who was over the house.”
Heb “the one who was over the city.”
Or “elders.”
Heb “servants.”
Heb “Do what is good in your eyes.”

verses.zh: 耶户又给他们写信说：「你们若归顺我，听从我的话，明日这时候，要将你们主人众子的首级带到耶斯列来见我。」那时王的儿子七十人都住在教养他们那城中的尊贵人家里。
verses.en: He wrote them a second letter, saying, “If you are really on my side and are willing to obey me,[NOTE:1] then take the heads of your master’s sons and come to me in Jezreel at this time tomorrow.”[NOTE:2] Now the king had 70 sons, and the prominent men[NOTE:3] of the city were raising them.
notes: Heb “If you are mine and you are listening to my voice.”

Jehu’s command is intentionally vague. Does he mean that they should bring the guardians (those who are “heads” over Ahab’s sons) for a meeting, or does he mean that they should bring the literal heads of Ahab’s sons with them (so reads Lucian’s Greek translation, the Syriac Peshitta, and some mss of the Targum)? The city leaders interpret his words in the literal sense, but Jehu’s command is so ambiguous he is able to deny complicity in the executions (see v. 9).
Heb “great men,” probably in wealth, position, and prestige.
verses.commentary:
10:6 "take the heads of the men, your master's sons, and come to me at Jezreel tomorrow about this time"
Beheading was a common practice of the day from the Assyrian documents. Jezreel was about 20 miles from Samaria,
which meant that these guardians had to act immediately to fulfill Jehu's request, without time to think.

verses.zh: 信一到，他们就把王的七十个儿子杀了，将首级装在筐里，送到在耶斯列的耶户那里。
verses.en: When they received the letter, they seized the king’s sons and executed all 70 of them.[NOTE:1] They put their heads in baskets and sent them to him in Jezreel.
notes: Heb “and when the letter came to them, they took the sons of the king and slaughtered seventy men.”

verses.zh: 有使者来告诉耶户说：「他们将王众子的首级送来了。」耶户说：「将首级在城门口堆作两堆，搁到明日。」
verses.en: The messenger came and told Jehu,[NOTE:1] “They have brought the heads of the king’s sons.” Jehu[NOTE:2] said, “Stack them in two piles at the entrance of the city gate until morning.”
notes: Heb “him”; the referent (Jehu) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (Jehu) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
10:8 "Put them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning" Jehu wanted to

- make a public display of the prophetic fulfillment of the fall of Ahab's house

- this was an action known in the ANE to discourage treason

▣ "heap" The root (BDB 840) is usually used of gathering grain into bundles after cutting. Here,
and only here, it is used of a pile of severed human heads.

verses.zh: 次日早晨，耶户出来，站着对众民说：「你们都是公义的，我背叛我主人，将他杀了；这些人却是谁杀的呢？
verses.en: In the morning he went out and stood there. Then he said to all the people, “You are innocent. I conspired against my master and killed him. But who struck down all of these men?
verses.commentary:
10:9 "you are innocent" Jehu is trying to remove the guilt of bloodshed (cf. Deut. 21:1-9). There is some
question whether the guardians themselves are later killed (v. 11). This is a specialized sense of the
ADJECTIVE "righteous" (BDB 843) as innocent (i.e., Gen. 20:4; Deut. 25:1; 1 Kgs. 8:32; 2 Chr. 6:23;
Prov. 17:15,26; 18:5). They (and he) are innocent because YHWH had ordered the death of Ahab's family.

verses.zh: 由此可知，耶和华指着亚哈家所说的话一句没有落空，因为耶和华藉他仆人以利亚所说的话都成就了。」
verses.en: Therefore take note that not one of the Lord’s words which he pronounced against Ahab’s dynasty[NOTE:1] will fail to materialize.[NOTE:2] The Lord has done what he announced through his servant Elijah.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the house of Ahab.”
Heb “will fall to the earth.”
Heb “by the hand of his servant Elijah.”
verses.commentary:
10:10 "Know then that there shall fall to the earth nothing of the word of the Lord"
This is an idiom (cf. Josh. 21:45; 23:14; 1 Sam. 3:19; 1 Kgs. 8:56) of the trustworthiness of YHWH's revelations
(NIDOTTE, vol 3, p. 129, #3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

verses.zh: 凡亚哈家在耶斯列所剩下的人和他的大臣、密友、祭司，耶户尽都杀了，没有留下一个。
verses.en: Then Jehu killed all who were left of Ahab’s family in Jezreel, and all his nobles, close friends, and priests. He left no survivors.
verses.commentary:
10:11 Notice the different people connected to the house of Omri that Jehu killed.

- all his great men

- all his acquaintances

- all his priests

- from vv. 1-8, all the kings "sons," which included all relatives

verses.zh: 耶户起身往撒马利亚去。在路上、牧人剪羊毛之处，
verses.en: Jehu then left there and set out for Samaria.[NOTE:1] While he was traveling through Beth Eked of the Shepherds,
notes: Heb “and he arose and went and came to Samaria.”
verses.commentary:
10:12 "Beth-eked" The place name (BDB 112) means "the house of binding." This refers to the place where the
sheep were sheared and during the process their feet were bound.

verses.zh: 遇见犹大王亚哈谢的弟兄，问他们说：「你们是谁？」回答说：「我们是亚哈谢的弟兄，现在下去要问王和太后的众子安。」
verses.en: Jehu encountered[NOTE:1] the relatives[NOTE:2] of King Ahaziah of Judah. He asked, “Who are you?” They replied, “We are Ahaziah’s relatives. We have come down to see how[NOTE:3] the king’s sons and the queen mother’s sons are doing.”
notes: Heb “found.”
Or “brothers.”
Heb “for the peace of.”
verses.commentary:
10:13 "Jehu met the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah" King Ahaziah was a grandson of Jezebel and part of
the prophet's prediction about the destruction of Ahab's entire house. We learn of the fate of most of his family from
2 Chr. 21:17; 22:1. Apparently these were 42 of his nephews (cf. 2 Chr. 22:8) who had not heard of the slaughter.

▣ "the queen mother" This refers to Jezebel.

verses.zh: 耶户吩咐说：「活捉他们！」跟从的人就活捉了他们，将他们杀在剪羊毛之处的坑边，共四十二人，没有留下一个。
verses.en: He said, “Capture them alive!” So they captured them alive and then executed all 42 of them by the cistern at Beth Eked. He left no survivors.

verses.zh: 耶户从那里前行，恰遇利甲的儿子约拿达来迎接他，耶户问他安，对他说：「你诚心待我像我诚心待你吗？」约拿达回答说：「是。」耶户说：「若是这样，你向我伸手」，他就伸手；耶户拉他上车。
verses.en: When he left there, he met[NOTE:1] Jehonadab son of Rekab who had been looking for him.[NOTE:2] Jehu greeted him and asked,[NOTE:3] “Are you as committed to me as I am to you?”[NOTE:4] Jehonadab answered, “I am!” Jehu replied, “If so, give me your hand.”[NOTE:5] So he offered his hand and Jehu[NOTE:6] pulled him up into the chariot.
notes: Heb “found.”
Heb “and he went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rekab [who was coming] to meet him.”
Heb “and he blessed him and said to him.”
Heb “Is there with your heart [what is] right, as my heart [is] with your heart?”

Heb “Jehonadab said, ‘There is and there is. Give your hand.’” If the text is allowed to stand, there are two possible ways to understand the syntax of וָיֵשׁ (vayesh), “and there is”: (1) The repetition of יֵשׁ (yesh, “there is and there is”) could be taken as emphatic, “indeed I am.” In this case, the entire statement could be taken as Jehonadab’s words or one could understand the words “give your hand” as Jehu’s. In the latter case the change in speakers is unmarked. (2) וָיֵשׁ begins Jehu’s response and has a conditional force, “if you are.” In this case, the transition in speakers is unmarked. However, it is possible that וַיֹּאמֶר (vayyoʾmer), “and he said,” or וַיֹּאמֶר יֵהוּא (vayyoʾmer yehu), “and Jehu said,” originally appeared between יֵשׁ and וָיֵשׁ and has accidentally dropped from the text by homoioarcton (note that both the proposed וַיֹּאמֶר and וָיֵשׁ begin with vav, ו). The present translation assumes such a textual reconstruction; it is supported by the LXX, Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate.
Heb “he”; the referent (Jehu) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
10:15 "Jehonadab the son of Rechab" We learn more of this unique tribal group from 1 Chr. 2:55 and Jer. 35:1-19
(NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 1126-1127). They are related to Moses' father-in-law, Jethro (cf. Genesis 18), apparently Kenites or
Midianites. They were strict "YHWHists" and nomads. They are present in the northern ten tribes in Jdgs. 4:17-22.
Josephus, Antiq. 9.6.6, says "Jehu and Jehonadab who had been his friend of old." However, this tradition was never
mentioned in the Bible. See Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 14-15.

▣ "If it is, give me your hand" This idiom is used in several senses (NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 210, #3, b).

- friendship ‒ Gen. 38:28

- formal alliance ‒ Ezra 10:19; Lam. 5:6; Ezek. 17:18

- denotes loyalty ‒ 1 Chr. 29:24

In this context any one of the above could fit.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "heart" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART.

verses.zh: 耶户说：「你和我同去，看我为耶和华怎样热心」；于是请他坐在车上，
verses.en: Jehu[NOTE:1] said, “Come with me and see how zealous I am for the Lord’s cause.”[NOTE:2] So he[NOTE:3] took him along in his chariot.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Jehu) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and see my zeal for the Lord.”
The MT has a plural form, but this is most likely an error. The LXX, Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate all have the singular.
verses.commentary:
10:16 "Come with me and see my zeal for the Lord" This shows the faith of
Jehonadab and the stated purpose of Jehu's actions.

▣ "he" The MT has the PLURAL but the LXX, Peshitta, and Vulgate have the
SINGULAR.

verses.zh: 到了撒马利亚，就把撒马利亚的亚哈家剩下的人都杀了，直到灭尽，正如耶和华对以利亚所说的。
verses.en: He went to Samaria and killed each of Ahab’s remaining family members who were in Samaria until he destroyed them,[NOTE:1] in keeping with the Lord’s message which he had announced to Elijah.
notes: Heb “him.” The pronoun refers to Ahab who represents his entire family.
verses.commentary: 10:17 It is uncertain who of Ahab and Jezebel's family, friends, servants remained.

verses.zh: 耶户招聚众民，对他们说：「亚哈事奉巴力还冷淡，耶户却更热心。
verses.en: Jehu assembled all the people and said to them, “Ahab worshiped[NOTE:1] Baal a little; Jehu will worship[NOTE:2] him with great devotion.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “served.
Or “serve.”
Heb “much” or “greatly.”
verses.commentary:
10:18-24 This was a calculated plot by Jehu to gather and destroy all the priests and followers of Ba'al.
Ba'al was the male fertility god of Canaan and Phoenicia.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY
WORSHIP OF THE ANE

verses.zh: 现在我要给巴力献大祭。应当叫巴力的众先知和一切拜巴力的人，并巴力的众祭司，都到我这里来，不可缺少一个；凡不来的必不得活。」耶户这样行，是用诡计要杀尽拜巴力的人。
verses.en: So now, bring to me all the prophets of Baal, as well as all his servants and priests.[NOTE:1] None of them must be absent, for I am offering a great sacrifice to Baal. Any of them who fails to appear will lose his life.” But Jehu was tricking them[NOTE:2] so he could destroy the servants of Baal.
notes: Heb “and now, all the prophets of Baal, all his servants and all his priests summon to me.”
Heb “acted with deception [or, ‘trickery’].”
verses.commentary:
10:19 "all the prophets of Baal. . .all his priests" There was a role distinction made between priests and
prophets both in Egypt and in Phoenicia. There seems to be a distinction made in the OT (cf. 1 Kgs. 18:19; 22:6).
Ba'al and Asherah were worshiped in every locality, on every high hill, throughout Canaan. Ahab had
constructed one large temple in Samaria. It was to this central shrine that all local priests and prophets were
summoned to a special royal inauguration service where Ba'al was to be acknowledged as the god of Israel
(i.e., vv. 18-19). This did not include local adherents to Ba'al and Asherah because no building was
big enough for that. These were the leaders.

verses.zh: 耶户说：「要为巴力宣告严肃会！」于是宣告了。
verses.en: Then Jehu ordered, “Make arrangements for[NOTE:1] a celebration for Baal.” So they announced it.
notes: Heb “set apart”; or “observe as holy.”

verses.zh: 耶户差人走遍以色列地；凡拜巴力的人都来齐了，没有一个不来的。他们进了巴力庙，巴力庙中从前边直到后边都满了人。
verses.en: Jehu sent invitations throughout Israel, and all the servants of Baal came; not one was absent. They arrived at the temple of Baal and filled it up from end to end.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the house of Baal was filled mouth to mouth.”
verses.commentary:
10:21 "the house of Baal" Ahab built this large temple in Samaria (cf. 1 Kgs. 16:32).

▣ "filled from one end to the other" The MT has the idiom "mouth to mouth" (BDB 805, #5) here, meaning
"extremity" or "end-to-end."

- of a temple ‒ here

- of a city ‒ 2 Kgs. 21:16

- of a land ‒ Ezra 9:11

verses.zh: 耶户吩咐掌管礼服的人说：「拿出礼服来，给一切拜巴力的人穿。」他就拿出礼服来给了他们。
verses.en: Jehu ordered the one who was in charge of the wardrobe,[NOTE:1] “Bring out robes for all the servants of Baal.” So he brought out robes for them.
notes: Heb “and he said to the one who was over the wardrobe.”
verses.commentary:
10:22 "wardrobe" This term (BDB 547, KB 594) appears only here and possibly Jer. 38:11. Apparently there
were special garments that signified a purification process. Their color is uncertain but in some cases, Ba'al
priests wore black robes (cf. Zephaniah 1). The Tyndale Commentary (OT) suggests "red" or "white." This
could refer to

- a robe

- a vestment (BDB 528)

- other special clerical garment

verses.zh: 耶户和利甲的儿子约拿达进了巴力庙，对拜巴力的人说：「你们察看察看，在你们这里不可有耶和华的仆人，只可容留拜巴力的人。」
verses.en: Then Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rekab went to the temple of Baal. Jehu[NOTE:1] said to the servants of Baal, “Make sure there are no servants of the Lord here with you; there must be only servants of Baal.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Jehu) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Search carefully and observe so that there are not here with you any servants of the Lord, but only the servants of Baal.”

verses.zh: 耶户和约拿达进去，献平安祭和燔祭。耶户先安派八十人在庙外，吩咐说：「我将这些人交在你们手中，若有一人脱逃，谁放的必叫他偿命！」
verses.en: They went inside to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed 80 men outside. He had told them, “If any of the men inside gets away, you will pay with your lives!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The man who escapes from the men whom I am bringing into your hands, [it will be] his life in place of his life.”
verses.commentary:
10:24 "shall give up his life in exchange" The Hebrew word for "life" is nephesh. If a guard
lost his prisoner he must take the penalty himself.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

verses.zh: 耶户献完了燔祭，就出来吩咐护卫兵和众军长说：「你们进去杀他们，不容一人出来！」护卫兵和军长就用刀杀他们，将尸首抛出去，便到巴力庙的城去了，
verses.en: When he finished offering the burnt sacrifice, Jehu ordered the royal guard[NOTE:1] and officers, “Come in and strike them down! Don’t let any escape!” So the royal guard and officers struck them down with the sword and left their bodies lying there.[NOTE:2] Then they entered the inner sanctuary of the temple of Baal.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “runners.”
Heb “and they threw.” No object appears. According to M. Cogan and H. Tadmor (II Kings [AB], 116), this is an idiom for leaving a corpse unburied.

Heb “and they came to the city of the house of Baal.” It seems unlikely that a literal city is meant. Some emend עִיר (ʿir), “city,” to דְּבִיר (devir) “holy place,” or suggest that עִיר is due to dittography of the immediately preceding עַד (ʿad) “to.” Perhaps עִיר is here a technical term meaning “fortress” or, more likely, “inner room.”
verses.commentary:
10:25 "threw them out" This VERB (BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil
IMPERFECT with waw) is an idiom for the slain bodies of the Ba'al
worshipers being taken outside the Ba'al temple and left unburied (cf. 1 Kgs. 13:25; Isa. 14:19).

verses.zh: 将巴力庙中的柱像都拿出来烧了；
verses.en: They hauled out the sacred pillar of the temple of Baal and burned it.
verses.commentary:
10:26 "pillars of the house of Baal and burned them" We learn from archaeology that the Phoenician pantheon
was represented by smooth conical stones with no carving. The phrase "and burned them" must relate to the Asherah
which was next to the pillars of Ba'al, which was the female symbol, a carved wooden stake or possibly
olive tree (i.e., Asherah).

verses.zh: 毁坏了巴力柱像，拆毁了巴力庙作为厕所，直到今日。
verses.en: They demolished[NOTE:1] the sacred pillar of Baal and[NOTE:2] the temple of Baal; it is used as[NOTE:3] a latrine[NOTE:4] to this very day.
notes: Or “pulled down.”
The verb “they demolished” is repeated in the Hebrew text.
Heb “and they made it into.”

The consonantal text (Kethib) has the hapax legomenon מַחֲרָאוֹת (makharaʾot), “places to defecate” or “dung houses” (note the related noun חֶרֶא (khereʾ)/חֲרִי (khari), “dung,” HALOT 348-49 s.v. *חֲרָאִים). The marginal reading (Qere) glosses this, perhaps euphemistically, מוֹצָאוֹת (motsaʾot), “outhouses.”
verses.commentary:
10:27

NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA
"latrine"

NKJV
"a refuse dump"

REB
"a privy"

Peshitta
"a public toilet-room"

This root (BDB 351, KB 348) appears only here. It is the same consonants as "dung." It was a
cultural way in the ANE to curse a place and make it unclean. See NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 257.

▣ "to this day" This is a recurrent textual marker of a later editor or scribe.

verses.zh: 这样，耶户在以色列中灭了巴力。
verses.en: So Jehu eradicated Baal worship[NOTE:1] from Israel.
notes: Heb “destroyed Baal.”

verses.zh: 只是耶户不离开尼八的儿子耶罗波安使以色列人陷在罪里的那罪，就是拜伯特利和但的金牛犊。
verses.en: However, Jehu did not repudiate the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had encouraged Israel to commit; the golden calves remained in Bethel[NOTE:1] and Dan.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
Heb “Except the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he caused Israel to commit, Jehu did not turn aside from after them—the golden calves which [were in] Bethel and which [were] in Dan.”
verses.commentary:
10:29 "the golden calves that were at Bethel and that were at Dan" All the prophets condemned
the golden calf worship set up by Jeroboam I (1 Kgs. 12:25-33; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 320). It was not that they were
initially idolatrous (cf. 1 Kgs. 12:28-29) but they

- broke the commandment of no graven images of Deity

- split the worship of YHWH away from Jerusalem (i.e., the place YHWH caused His name to dwell)

verses.zh: 耶和华对耶户说：「因你办好我眼中看为正的事，照我的心意待亚哈家，你的子孙必接续你坐以色列的国位，直到四代。」
verses.en: The Lord said to Jehu, “You have done well. You have accomplished my will and carried out my wishes with regard to Ahab’s dynasty. Therefore four generations of your descendants will rule over Israel.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Jehu ruled over Israel from approximately 841-814 b.c. Four of his descendants (Jehoahaz, Jehoash, Jeroboam II, and Zechariah) ruled from approximately 814-753 b.c. The dynasty came to an end when Shallum assassinated Zechariah in 753 b.c. See 2 Kgs 15:8-12. tn Heb “Because you have done well by doing what is proper in my eyes—according to all which was in my heart you have done to the house of Ahab—sons of four generations will sit for you on the throne of Israel.” In the Hebrew text the Lord’s statement is one long sentence (with a parenthesis). The translation above divides it into shorter sentences for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
10:30 "My eyes. . .My heart" This is anthropomorphic language to describe Israel's Deity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

verses.zh: 只是耶户不尽心遵守耶和华―以色列　神的律法，不离开耶罗波安使以色列人陷在罪里的那罪。
verses.en: But Jehu did not carefully and wholeheartedly obey the law of the Lord God of Israel.[NOTE:1] He did not repudiate the sins which Jeroboam had encouraged Israel to commit.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart.”
Heb “He did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam which he caused Israel to commit.”
verses.commentary:
10:31 Jehu, like many of the kings of Israel and Judah, started off well but did not

- follow YHWH with a whole heart

- follow YHWH all their lives

verses.zh: 在那些日子，耶和华才割裂以色列国，使哈薛攻击以色列的境界，
verses.en: In those days the Lord began to reduce the size of Israel’s territory.[NOTE:1] Hazael attacked their eastern border.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “began to cut off Israel.”
Heb “Hazael struck them down in all the territory of Israel, from the Jordan on the east.” In the Hebrew text the phrase “from the Jordan on the east” begins v. 33.
verses.commentary:
10:32 "Hazael" He is mentioned on the Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III as a very stubborn military adversary
of Assyria. We learn of Shalmaneser III's advance even as far as the seacoast of Judah from 2 Kgs. 12:17-18.

verses.zh: 乃是约旦河东、基列全地，从靠近亚嫩谷边的亚罗珥起，就是基列和巴珊的迦得人、流便人、玛拿西人之地。
verses.en: He conquered all the land of Gilead, including the territory of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh, extending all the way from the Aroer in the Arnon Valley through Gilead to Bashan.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassehites, from Aroer which is near the Arnon Valley, and Gilead, and Bashan.”
verses.commentary: 10:33 Israel lost the entire trans-Jordan area by YHWH's direction (v. 32).

verses.zh: 耶户其余的事，凡他所行的和他的勇力都写在以色列诸王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Jehu’s reign, including all his accomplishments and successes, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Jehu, and all which he did and all his strength, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”
verses.commentary:
10:34 "all his might" This is a very unusual phrase to describe Israeli kings. It is unusual in that it is used
of a man who had such major military losses. We learn from the Black Obelisk that tribute was paid by Jehu to
Assyria.

verses.zh: 耶户与他列祖同睡，葬在撒马利亚；他儿子约哈斯接续他作王。
verses.en: Jehu passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried in Samaria.[NOTE:2] His son Jehoahaz replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 耶户在撒马利亚作以色列王二十八年。
verses.en: Jehu reigned over Israel for 28 years in Samaria.
verses.commentary:
10:36 "twenty-eight years" This was one of the longest, most stable reigns in Israel. The only longer reign
was that of Jeroboam II that lasted 41 years.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is Jehu condemned by the prophet Hosea (Hos. 1:4) for what seems to be predicted prophecy concerning the
house of Ahab? (See Hard Sayings of the Bible, p. 236, and Gleason Archer, Encyclopedia of Bible
Difficulties, pp. 207-209)

- Why did Jehu not want to kill Ahab's sons in Samaria?

- Why did Jehu want the support of Jehonadab, the son of Rachab? (v. 15)

- Why was Jehu so concerned about Ba'al worship but not concerned about the golden calf worship?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- The military coup performed by Jehu was instigated and predicted by both the prophets, Elijah, 1 Kgs. 21:21,29;
and Elisha, 2 Kings 9.

- The year of this revolt seems to be 842 B.C.

- The rabbis say that Jehu was of the tribe of Manesseh, fulfilling Gen. 48:19.

1Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria,
to the rulers of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of the children of Ahab, saying, 2"Now,
when this letter comes to you, since your master's sons are with you, as well as the chariots and horses
and a fortified city and the weapons, 3select the best and fittest of your master's sons, and
set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house." 4But they feared greatly
and said, "Behold, the two kings did not stand before him; how then can we stand?" 5And
the one who was over the household, and he who was over the city, the elders, and the guardians of
the children, sent word to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants, all that you say to us we will do, we will not
make any man king; do what is good in your sight." 6Then he wrote a letter to them a
second time saying, "If you are on my side, and you will listen to my voice, take the heads of the men,
your master's sons, and come to me at Jezreel tomorrow about this time." Now the king's sons, seventy
persons, were with the great men of the city, who were rearing them. 7When the letter
came to them, they took the king's sons and slaughtered them, seventy persons, and put their heads
in baskets, and sent them to him at Jezreel. 8When the messenger came and told him,
saying, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons," he said, "Put them in two heaps at the
entrance of the gate until morning." 9Now in the morning he went out and stood and
said to all the people, "You are innocent; behold, I conspired against my master and killed him, but
who killed all these? 10Know then that there shall fall to the earth nothing of the word
of the Lord, which the Lord spoke
concerning the house of Ahab, for the Lord has done what He spoke
through His servant Elijah." 11So Jehu killed all who remained of the house of Ahab in
Jezreel, and all his great men and his acquaintances and his priests, until he left him without a survivor.
